name: Purplish Blue
lede: Purplish Blue is a descriptive name, not a historical one: it says a blue leans toward purple, and the books use it for many different blues.

sections.title: A phrase, not a pigment
sections.body:
Paterson uses *purplish blue* to define, among others, periwinkle, Winsor blue, Copenhagen blue, hyacinth blue and Scotch blue [1]. Each describes a different shade: a light one for periwinkle blue, a bright one for Copenhagen blue, a dark one for navy blue [1]. Egyptian blue, the ancient copper-lime-quartz pigment, is a rich purplish blue or turquoise in his entry [1]. Gage describes the Virgin in a purplish-blue mantle, probably painted in ultramarine, in a diptych that follows the traditional Italian fashion [2].

So the phrase carries a hue direction, and nothing about lightness. See [[periwinkle-blue]], [[navy]], [[hyacinth-blue]], [[scotch-blue]] and [[egyptian-blue]].

sections.title: This swatch
sections.body: The swatch here is #601EF9, from the xkcd color survey, and it is far more saturated than any of the dictionary shades [3]. It sits 3.9 units from [[violet]] and is a near twin of Purply Blue, 1.5 apart [3]. The closest neighbor in our own list is [[burple]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At the default threshold the swatch is too saturated to match; at fifteen units 47 of 23,781 archive paintings carry it over at least five per cent of the canvas [4]. They include a Rajput-school [[painting:cma-314425|Krishna and the cowherds]] of about 1640 at 34 per cent, and Henry Ottmann's [[painting:commons-Q17496146|The Luxembourg Station in Brussels]] of 1903 at 27 per cent [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the colors are as photographed [4].

questions.q: Paterson uses purplish blue for navy and for Copenhagen blue.

openers: Navy, Copenhagen and Scotch blue are all 'purplish blue' in one dictionary, in different lightnesses.

issues: Gage's purplish-blue-mantle diptych is in the traditional Italian fashion (attributed to Benedetto di Bindo), not Netherlandish; fixed.
